SECTION: FLCR01 §4 — four candidate criteria, compared on scientific meaning
SCIENTIFIC_OBJECT: persistence of an ORGANISING LINEAGE through material turnover -- not preservation of an arbitrary particle identifier

FOUNDER_SURVIVAL.meaning: the exact initial Y particle is still alive at T_HORIZON (the old C2)
FOUNDER_SURVIVAL.why: the X cloud already turns over completely; the whole programme is about a structure that persists while its material is replaced. Requiring one tagged particle to persist imposes on Y precisely the property the project denies is required of X. It is a particle-identity criterion wearing an organisational label.
FOUNDER_SURVIVAL.aggregate_engine_can_identify: only while nY == 1; once two Y share a cell the engine cannot say which is the founder
FOUNDER_SURVIVAL.consequence_for_the_region: forces muY <= 6.30e-05 and is what makes the region empty for every kY and every exposure
FOUNDER_SURVIVAL.architectural_requirement: a per-particle identity the physics does not carry

LINEAGE_NON_EXTINCTION.meaning: at least one Y descended from the initial state is present at T_HORIZON; the founder may die after producing a successor
LINEAGE_NON_EXTINCTION.why: this is the minimal statement of continuity through turnover, and it is exactly the property the project claims for the X structure
LINEAGE_NON_EXTINCTION.why_not_sufficient: non-extinction says nothing about spatial organisation; a single wandering Y satisfies it
LINEAGE_NON_EXTINCTION.aggregate_engine_can_identify: yes -- N_Y > 0 is a total count and needs no genealogy
LINEAGE_NON_EXTINCTION.consequence_for_the_region: removes the muY upper bound entirely; the C1-versus-C3 contradiction dissolves

ORGANISER_CONTINUITY.meaning: at every required time at least one Y occupies or controls a source-bound organising centre, whatever the particle
ORGANISER_CONTINUITY.why: continuity of FUNCTION is the claim; continuity of count is only its shadow
ORGANISER_CONTINUITY.why_not_sufficient: one centre is not the two-centre object under test
ORGANISER_CONTINUITY.aggregate_engine_can_identify: yes -- a centre is a single-linkage cluster of occupied Y cells at radius CORE_R, plus the local X response, both recorded every step
ORGANISER_CONTINUITY.consequence_for_the_region: adds a function requirement on top of non-extinction

TWO_CENTRE_FUNCTIONAL_CONTINUITY.meaning: after first separation, two spatially distinct Y organising centres persist for a frozen hold duration, each retaining a qualified local X response, without a premature third centre
TWO_CENTRE_FUNCTIONAL_CONTINUITY.why: this IS the object the programme set out to detect; it is the operational form of 'one organising centre became two and both kept working'
TWO_CENTRE_FUNCTIONAL_CONTINUITY.aggregate_engine_can_identify: yes -- n_centres, per-centre occupancy, per-cell local nX/nSY/free and pairwise distances are all recorded every step
TWO_CENTRE_FUNCTIONAL_CONTINUITY.consequence_for_the_region: replaces C3's prohibition of a second centre with a hold requirement plus a third-centre prohibition

WHY_NOT_CHOSEN_FOR_CREATING_A_REGION: the choice is made from the scientific object, and it can be stated without reference to any region: the programme tests whether an organising structure persists while its material is replaced. A criterion that fails the moment the original particle is replaced contradicts the hypothesis it is meant to test. That argument would stand even if founder survival happened to admit a wide region.
IF_FOUNDER_IDENTITY_WERE_ESSENTIAL: it would be essential only for a claim about an individual rather than a lineage -- for instance 'this particular organiser survived a perturbation'. No such claim is in scope, and the programme forbids reproduction and heredity claims outright.
NO_INVENTED_GENEALOGY: none of the three retained criteria requires knowing which Y produced which. All are functions of total count, cell occupancy, cluster structure and local fields -- every one of them recorded. Where genealogy would be needed it is declared unidentifiable rather than imputed.
